Definition: from G1223 and G5083; to watch thoroughly, i.e. (positively and transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to avoid wholly:--keep.
BiblicalUsage: To keep is to hold a thing safe, and the word is used of Mary keeping all these sayings in her heart and of the Gentile believers keeping themselves from idols. One keeps by treasuring, the other by turning away, and both are the keeping of faith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe keeping is the quiet work of a lifetime; Mary kept the words in her heart until their meaning opened, and the church keeps itself from idols by the same patience, holding fast what is good and letting go of what is not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
